drug_class: Combined hormonal oral contraceptive (birth control pill)
purpose: This medication is a combination birth control pill used to prevent pregnancy. It may also be prescribed to help regulate periods, reduce menstrual cramps, or treat acne. Some forms are designed so you only have your period four times a year instead of monthly.
how_it_works: This pill contains two hormones — estrogen and progestin — that work together to prevent pregnancy in a few ways. First, they stop your ovaries from releasing an egg each month. They also thicken the mucus in your cervix so sperm have a harder time getting through, and they change the lining of your uterus to make it less likely for a fertilized egg to attach.
common_side_effects: Nausea, headache, breast tenderness or swelling, spotting or light bleeding between periods (especially in the first few months), mood changes, decreased sex drive, and bloating. These often improve after the first two or three months.
warnings: This pill is not recommended if you smoke and are over 35, as it raises the risk of serious blood clots, stroke, or heart attack. Tell your doctor if you have a history of blood clots, high blood pressure, migraines with aura, liver problems, or certain cancers. It does NOT protect against sexually transmitted infections (STIs).
typical_dosing: You take one pill by mouth every day at roughly the same time each day. Depending on the pack, you may take active hormone pills for 21, 84, or 91 days followed by placebo or low-dose pills. Try to take it at the same time each day to make it most effective.
